title: Laredo's Marco Raya Reflects on MLB Debut, 2026 Season with Twins
excerpt: Laredo's Marco Raya made his major league debut with the Minnesota Twins on June 27, 2026, becoming the youngest Laredo native to reach the big leagues. The 24-year-old right-hander looks back on a season of firsts — and a shoulder injury that cut his time in the majors short.
content:
⚾ LAREDO SPORTS

Laredo's Marco Raya reached the major leagues this year, making his debut for the Minnesota Twins on June 27, 2026, against the Colorado Rockies at Target Field — becoming the youngest Laredo native to play in the majors and the fourth Laredo-born player to get there.

Raya, a 24-year-old right-hander and United South High School graduate, was drafted by Minnesota in the fourth round of the 2020 draft. He spent four minor-league seasons as a starter before moving to the bullpen late in 2025, a role he kept through 2026.

His first big-league outing lasted two innings, with two runs on two hits and two walks and one strikeout. He followed it with two scoreless two-inning appearances — June 30 against the Houston Astros and July 4 against the New York Yankees.

The road to the call-up ran through Triple-A St. Paul, where Raya started the season rough: 16 earned runs in 13 1/3 innings over 10 games in March and April. He turned it around from there, posting a 2.81 ERA over his next 25 2/3 innings before Minnesota called him up on June 24.

After his three big-league outings, a right shoulder impingement put Raya on the 15-day injured list. Once he recovered, he returned to Triple-A, where he finished the season as other Twins relievers came back to the big-league bullpen.

Raya called the debut euphoric, saying he can still close his eyes and picture stepping onto the mound and taking it all in before his first inning. He said the move to the bullpen was rocky at first — a starter gets all the time in the world to prepare, while a reliever has to be ready in five pitches — but he adjusted and built a routine that worked.

He said the injury was more of a blow mentally than physically, since he had dealt with the same issue a few years earlier and knew how to recover from it. This offseason he is focusing on his mechanics over the rubber and on being more consistent with his misses, after spending past offseasons building strength and size. He said he felt he had a really good year overall and is looking forward to doing good things next year.

Sources: MLB Trade Rumors; Sports Illustrated; The Baseball Cube.
